items.label: PandaBreath / DragonBreath Chamber Heater
items.description: BIQU Panda Breath chamber heater and air filter integration, or DragonBreath open firmware on the same board.

auto.label: Panda Breath
auto.confirm:
WARNING: Panda Breath significantly raises sustained enclosure temperatures, accelerating wear on electronics, motors, and other components beyond their rated conditions. Any damage attributable to elevated thermal stress is unlikely to be covered under warranty. Additional motherboard cooling is required before use — see the documentation for details.

Before enabling Panda Breath auto mode, complete all of the following steps:

1. Install additional active cooling on the motherboard (see documentation).
2. Ensure the Panda Breath device is running firmware v1.0.3.
3. Configure a static DHCP lease for this printer on your router — the printer IP is embedded into the Panda Breath device and must not change after a reboot.
4. Configure a static DHCP lease for the Panda Breath device on your router — Klipper will connect to it by IP address on every print.
5. Power-cycle the Panda Breath device and wait at least 5 seconds before proceeding.
6. Enter the Panda Breath IP address in the field below.

Auto mode heats the chamber with Klipper first, then hands off hold and cool-down behaviour to Panda native auto mode.

(If you have flashed your Panda Breath with DragonBreath open firmware instead, use the DragonBreath option below.)

inputs.name: ACKNOWLEDGED
inputs.label: Type "I UNDERSTAND" to confirm you have read the documentation and accept the warranty and longevity risks

manual.label: Panda Breath (Manual mode)
manual.confirm:
WARNING: Panda Breath significantly raises sustained enclosure temperatures, accelerating wear on electronics, motors, and other components beyond their rated conditions. Any damage attributable to elevated thermal stress is unlikely to be covered under warranty. Additional motherboard cooling is required before use — see the documentation for details.

Before enabling Panda Breath manual mode, complete all of the following steps:

1. Install additional active cooling on the motherboard (see documentation).
2. Ensure the Panda Breath device is running firmware v1.0.3.
3. Configure a static DHCP lease for this printer on your router — the printer IP is embedded into the Panda Breath device and must not change after a reboot.
4. Configure a static DHCP lease for the Panda Breath device on your router — Klipper will connect to it by IP address on every print.
5. Power-cycle the Panda Breath device and wait at least 5 seconds before proceeding.
6. Enter the Panda Breath IP address in the field below.

Manual mode is a legacy fallback that may be less safe if the device or network connectivity is lost during a print.

inputs.name: ACKNOWLEDGED
inputs.label: Type "I UNDERSTAND" to confirm you have read the documentation and accept the warranty and longevity risks

dragonbreath.label: DragonBreath (Recommended)
dragonbreath.confirm:
WARNING: A chamber heater raises sustained enclosure temperatures, accelerating wear on electronics and motors beyond their rated conditions — likely NOT warranty-covered. Additional motherboard cooling is required (see docs).

DragonBreath is community open firmware for a MAINS-POWERED heater, flashed onto the same Panda Breath board. NO WARRANTY — a fault could cause overheating, fire, or damage. Use at your own risk; never run it unattended.

Before enabling:
1. Add active cooling to the motherboard (see docs).
2. Flash DragonBreath firmware onto the Panda Breath board and provision its Wi-Fi (see https://github.com/plastikman/DragonBreath).
3. Give the DragonBreath device a static DHCP lease — Klipper connects by IP.
4. Enter its IP below.

(If your Panda Breath is still running stock firmware, use the Panda Auto option above instead.)

Advanced: to use a device control token (NVS ctl_token), add a "token:" line to the DragonBreath config after enabling (see docs).

items.label: Touchscreen GUI (Experimental)
items.description: Select the interface shown on the printer's built-in touchscreen.

snapmaker.label: Snapmaker
snapmaker.confirm:
Switch back to the stock Snapmaker touchscreen UI?

The downloaded HelixScreen files are removed, so switching back to HelixScreen later downloads them again.

The printer reboots to apply the change.

helixscreen.label: HelixScreen
helixscreen.confirm:
Replace the stock Snapmaker touchscreen UI with HelixScreen?

HelixScreen is a third-party Klipper touchscreen interface and is downloaded on demand (~46 MB). It manages WiFi itself, but reads and writes the same saved-network file as the stock UI, so an already-configured network carries over automatically.

The printer reboots to apply the change.

items.label: Force Bed Mesh Calibration
items.description: Forces bed mesh calibration before each print.

force.label: Force Full Mesh
force.confirm: Force full bed mesh calibration before every print?

adaptive.label: Force Adaptive Mesh
adaptive.confirm: Force adaptive bed mesh calibration before every print? Falls back to full mesh when exclude_object is not active. Make sure to enable 'Exclude Object' in your slicer so Klipper receives object boundary data — without it, adaptive mesh always falls back to a full mesh.

items.label: Object Processing for Adaptive Mesh
items.description: Enables Moonraker object processing for adaptive mesh. Prefer enabling exclude object in your slicer instead.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.confirm: Enable Moonraker object processing? Note: Enabling 'Exclude Object' in your slicer settings is preferred over this option. This can cause long processing times for large gcode files (> 100MB), delays when uploading files, and extended time stuck at 100% in Snapmaker Orca. Only enable if your slicer doesn't support exclude object.

items.label: Force Timelapse
items.description: Forces timelapse regardless if configured in the Snapmaker app. Your slicer must call TIMELAPSE_START, TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME, and TIMELAPSE_STOP.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.confirm: Allow TIMELAPSE_START to bypass the Snapmaker timelapse preference? Your slicer must call TIMELAPSE_START, TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME, and TIMELAPSE_STOP.

items.label: Fan Curves
items.description: Select quieter nonlinear cooling curves for the power and nozzle fans. Nozzle fans follow actual nozzle temperature; the power fan starts at 70°C actual temperature with 5°C hysteresis and keeps the cavity guard.

quiet.label: Quiet
quiet.confirm:
Apply the Quiet fan curves?
Nozzle fans stay off below 50°C and ramp nonlinearly from actual temperature. The power fan starts at 70°C actual temperature, stops below 65°C, and ramps gently. The cavity guard is 55°C and 60%.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.confirm:
Apply the Balanced fan curves?
Nozzle fans stay off below 60°C and ramp earlier than Quiet. The power fan starts at 70°C actual temperature, stops below 65°C, and ramps with more cooling margin. The cavity guard is 55°C and 60%.

stock.label: Stock
stock.confirm: Restore the original Snapmaker fan curves?

items.label: Max Speed
items.description: Experimental. Raises the XY motion limits and speeds up tool changes. Increases wear on your printer and can cause print problems such as Z skipping. Balanced is the recommended starting point, and a calibrated printer is required.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.confirm:
WARNING: EXPERIMENTAL. Raises XY velocity to 600 mm/s (stock 500), tool changes to 550 mm/s and dock grab to 30 mm/s.
This runs the printer past its rated limits. It increases wear on your printer and can cause print problems such as Z skipping, layer shifts, and ringing.
Only enable on a fully calibrated printer with tool changes already reliable at stock speeds. Set this back to Disabled if prints degrade.

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive.confirm:
WARNING: EXPERIMENTAL — highest tier. Raises XY velocity to 750 mm/s (stock 500), tool changes to 700 mm/s and dock grab to 50 mm/s.
This runs the printer well past its rated limits. It increases wear on your printer and can cause print problems such as Z skipping, layer shifts, and ringing.
Only enable on a fully calibrated printer with tool changes already reliable at stock speeds. Drop back if prints degrade.

items.label: TMC AutoTune
items.description: Optimizes TMC2240 driver settings for quieter operation and better performance.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.confirm: Enable TMC AutoTune? This optimizes TMC2240 driver settings for quieter operation and better performance. Monitor motor temperatures, print quality, and skipped steps during first use.

items.label: TMC Reduced Current
items.description: Lowers X/Y motor current from 1.2A to 1.0A for quieter operation and less heat.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.confirm: Enable TMC Reduced Current? This lowers X/Y motor current from 1.2A to 1.0A for quieter operation and less heat. Monitor motor temperatures and print quality after enabling.

items.label: Toolhead 1
items.description: Temporary thermistor, heating, and MCU bypass for Toolhead 1.

bypass_thermistor.label: Bypass Thermistor
bypass_thermistor.confirm: Apply the faulty toolhead bypass to Toolhead 1? This disables normal temperature fault handling for Toolhead 1 so the printer can keep using the other toolheads. Do not heat or print with the faulty toolhead while this bypass is enabled.

bypass_mcu.label: Bypass MCU (Disconnected)
bypass_mcu.confirm: Apply the MCU bypass to Toolhead 1? Use this only if Toolhead 1's board is dead or its cable is disconnected. This makes Toolhead 1's stepper and heater fully inert - it cannot move, extrude, or heat at all - but lets the printer boot and keep using the other toolheads.
